name: Halloween Solar Storms 2003
historicalImpact: Over 47 satellites reported orbital anomalies, star tracker blindness, and memory upsets. The Japanese ADEOS-2 science satellite suffered permanent electrical power system failure. Mars Odyssey MARIE radiation instrument was permanently disabled by heavy ion damage.
spacecraftCountermeasures: Stow high-gain antennas and orient spacecraft for minimum frontal cross-section
Power down non-essential scientific payloads and high-voltage sensors
Switch ADCS from optical star trackers to coarse sun-sensors + gyroscopes
Enable memory scrubbers and EDAC autonomous single-event-upset resets

name: March 1989 Hydro-Québec Storm
historicalImpact: Induced geomagnetically induced currents (GIC) collapsed the Hydro-Québec power grid in 90 seconds. Severe upper-atmospheric heating dramatically increased thermospheric density, causing LEO satellites to drop thousands of meters in altitude and throwing off thousands of space tracking radar tracks.
spacecraftCountermeasures: Command orbital drag reboost maneuvers using onboard chemical propulsion
Increase telemetry ground station pass frequency to re-acquire drifting ephemerides
Monitor battery charge-discharge cycles during extended atmospheric drag tumbling

name: July 2012 Ultra-Fast CME (Near-Carrington Event)
historicalImpact: Fastest coronal mass ejection ever measured in the space age, crossing the 1 AU distance in only 18.6 hours. The storm directly struck NASA's STEREO-A solar observatory, which survived and gathered unprecedented in-situ magnetic field and particle measurements. Had it erupted 9 days earlier, it would have struck Earth directly.
spacecraftCountermeasures: Immediate entry into hardened Safe Hold Mode
Isolate critical avionics buses and shunt solar array peak power strings
Activate redundant flight computer cold standby watchdogs
Execute scheduled autonomous reboot verification once proton flux drops below 100 pfu
